problem_description: Evaluate the definite integral of the function x·sin(2x) from x = 0 to x = π/8.

prerequisites.reason: The integrand is a product of a polynomial (x) and a trigonometric function (sin(2x)), which is a classic scenario for the integration-by-parts technique.
After finding an antiderivative, the fundamental theorem of calculus must be applied to compute the value between the given limits.
Recognising that the derivative of cos(2x) is −2 sin(2x) (and vice-versa) helps set up the integration by parts or substitution efficiently.

givens.explanation: These limits define the definite integral to be evaluated.
This is the function we must integrate.
